title: Standby Sanity Suite and Dependency Failure-Injection Rehearsal
creator: Jordan Li
description:
Goal: Build an automated 'Standby Sanity Suite' that runs scheduled rehearsals of active->passive failover with targeted dependency failure-injection. The suite validates end-to-end recovery fidelity (state, KV, tokenstore, routing), SLO preservation under progressive load shedding, and circuit-breaker behavior for dependent services. Purpose is to create a repeatable, low-risk rehearsal that surface regressions early and produces measurable pass/fail signals for runbooks and SLIs.

Scope: This ticket covers the test harness, orchestration playbook for the rehearsal, core verification probes (data integrity, request-path latency percentiles, error budgets), and a small set of chaos experiments (eg. NFS latencies, DB read-only mode, control-plane partition). It does not replace full operator-led DR cutovers; it augments them with automated checks and telemetry.

Success criteria for this ticket: harness merged, one scheduled rehearsal configured in staging, dashboards and CI gates created, and a first successful validation run with artifacts stored in the DR-run logs bucket.
acceptance_criteria: Standby Sanity Suite repo and CI pipeline merged to infra/standby-sanity with README + run instructions
One scheduled rehearsal runs weekly in staging and writes structured results to s3://redwood-dr-results/staging/2026-03
Automated probes validate KV snapshot parity within 60s window and tokenstore rehydration completes without data loss
Circuit-breakers and load-shedding thresholds exercise expected degradation modes; SLO regression detectors trigger alerts for >0.5% SLO drift
Playbook page (Confluence) with step-by-step escalation and rollback actions is reviewed and approved by SRE and Platform PMs
runbook_steps: Pre-check: Verify last successful backup and snapshot timestamp (tokenstore, KV snapshots) and persist checksums to artifacts store
Canary: Route 5% of synthetic traffic to passive region with read-only token to validate routing and prefix cache behavior
Inject 1: Simulate dependent service degradation (DB read-only) and assert circuit-breaker trips within configured 200ms bind threshold
Inject 2: Introduce 100-300ms network latency to storage layer and assert automatic load-shedding reduces non-critical paths per shedding policy
Failover step: Promote passive region into active routing for synthetic traffic and validate live traffic stays within SLO windows (p50,p95,p99) for 30 minutes
Validation: Run KV and tokenstore reconciliation tests; confirm snapshot delta < 0.1% and application-level data checks pass
Rollback: Trigger automated rollback by switching routing back to original active region and run post-rollback integrity checks
Postmortem gating: Collect logs, traces, and metrics; populate DR rehearsal checklist and open follow-up tickets for any failed assertions
monitoring_checks: SLO monitors: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms, error rate < 0.5% for synthetic workloads
KV consistency probe: checksum match between leader and standby snapshots within 60s window
Tokenstore validation: token issuance and revocation flows tested with end-to-end trace sample
Circuit-breaker telemetry: count of CB opens, average open duration, and downstream error amplification factor
Capacity signals: GPU utilization, queue length, and request latency per instance during promotion
rollback_plan: If SLOs breach defined thresholds for >5 minutes, abort promotion and initiate rollback to prior active region
If KV snapshot parity fails, pause traffic and initiate snapshot restore into quarantine cluster for manual verification
If tokenstore rehydration fails, revert service-level routing and trigger emergency tokenstore restore runbook (see ENG-24001)
If dependent service circuit breakers remain open for >15 minutes, execute dependency failover plan and notify DB-on-call
experiments: Gradual traffic ramp: 0% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 90 minutes to validate autoscaling and latency tails
Targeted dependency kill: Make specific downstream call return 503 and validate upstream CB behavior and fallbacks
State reconciliation test: Insert synthetic keys into leader before promotion and verify presence and TTLs after promotion
Load-shedding policy sweep: Test three shedding thresholds (conservative, default, aggressive) and measure cost/latency trade-offs
